entries.authors: Campbell, J. P., McCloy, R. A., Oppler, S. H., & Sager, C. E.
entries.title: A theory of performance
entries.venue: In N. Schmitt & W. C. Borman (Eds.), Personnel Selection in Organizations (pp. 35–70). Jossey-Bass
entries.main_finding: Defines performance as behaviour relevant to organisational goals that is under the individual's control, distinct from its results; proposes a multidimensional taxonomy (eight components, some job-specific).
entries.limitations: Theory chapter; the component structure is derived largely from military (Project A) data.
entries.relevance: Foundational distinction between behaviour, results and determinants.
entries.design_implications: MeritVector separates OUTCOMES (results) from CONTRIBUTION (the individual's role) and treats results as contaminated by factors outside the person's control.

entries.authors: Campbell, J. P., & Wiernik, B. M.
entries.title: The modeling and assessment of work performance
entries.venue: Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior, 2, 47–74
entries.main_finding: Reviews the substantive models of individual work performance and how performance is assessed, re-emphasising performance as behaviour and the difficulty of measuring it well.
entries.limitations: Narrative review; not specific to project-based knowledge work.
entries.relevance: Up-to-date synthesis for the construct definitions in the ontology.
entries.design_implications: Constructs are defined behaviourally with explicit indicators; outcome metrics are labelled as results, not performance.

entries.authors: Borman, W. C., & Motowidlo, S. J.
entries.title: Expanding the criterion domain to include elements of contextual performance
entries.venue: In N. Schmitt & W. C. Borman (Eds.), Personnel Selection in Organizations (pp. 71–98). Jossey-Bass
entries.main_finding: Distinguishes task performance (core technical work) from contextual performance (behaviours supporting the social and organisational environment).
entries.limitations: Chapter-level argument; empirical support comes from later studies.
entries.relevance: Project managers' value is heavily contextual (coordination, enabling others).
entries.design_implications: LEADERSHIP and collaboration are separate constructs from delivery outcomes; low evidence coverage for them is reported as a gap, not a deficit.

entries.authors: Motowidlo, S. J., & Van Scotter, J. R.
entries.title: Evidence that task performance should be distinguished from contextual performance
entries.main_finding: Task and contextual performance each contributed independently to supervisors' overall performance judgements; experience related more to task, personality more to contextual performance.
entries.limitations: US Air Force mechanics; supervisory ratings as the criterion.
entries.relevance: Supports multidimensional rather than single-score assessment.
entries.design_implications: No single composite merit score; dimensions are reported separately.

entries.authors: Podsakoff, P. M., MacKenzie, S. B., Paine, J. B., & Bachrach, D. G.
entries.title: Organizational citizenship behaviors: A critical review of the theoretical and empirical literature and suggestions for future research
entries.main_finding: Reviews OCB dimensions, antecedents and consequences and notes conceptual overlap among related constructs.
entries.limitations: Most evidence is cross-sectional and rating-based.
entries.relevance: Citizenship-type contributions (helping, enabling other teams) rarely appear in system-of-record data.
entries.design_implications: Evidence gaps for citizenship behaviours are expected; MeritVector does not infer their absence from missing records.

entries.authors: Pulakos, E. D., Arad, S., Donovan, M. A., & Plamondon, K. E.
entries.title: Adaptability in the workplace: Development of a taxonomy of adaptive performance
entries.main_finding: Proposes and supports an eight-dimension taxonomy of adaptive performance (e.g., dealing with uncertain or unpredictable work situations).
entries.limitations: Taxonomy derived from critical incidents; criterion-related evidence limited.
entries.relevance: Scope volatility and uncertain projects call for adaptive performance.
entries.design_implications: DEVELOPMENT and adaptation are measured as change under changing conditions (scope changes, complexity), not as raw output.

entries.authors: Griffin, M. A., Neal, A., & Parker, S. K.
entries.title: A new model of work role performance: Positive behavior in uncertain and interdependent contexts
entries.main_finding: Cross-classifies proficiency, adaptivity and proactivity at individual, team and organisation levels; uncertainty and interdependence shape which behaviours matter.
entries.limitations: Supervisor and self ratings; Australian samples.
entries.relevance: Directly motivates context variables (uncertainty, interdependence) and the individual/team/organisation split.
entries.design_implications: Contribution is recorded at individual, team and organisation level; attribution to individuals is explicit and reviewable.

entries.authors: Robinson, S. L., & Bennett, R. J.
entries.title: A typology of deviant workplace behavior: A multidimensional scaling study
entries.main_finding: Deviant workplace behaviours vary on minor–serious and interpersonal–organisational dimensions, giving four categories.
entries.limitations: Typology of perceived behaviours; not a measurement instrument for operational data.
entries.relevance: Counterproductive work behaviour is part of the performance domain.
entries.design_implications: Out of scope by design: MeritVector does not detect or score counterproductive behaviour from work data — that would require surveillance and invite false accusations.

entries.authors: Rotundo, M., & Sackett, P. R.
entries.title: The relative importance of task, citizenship, and counterproductive performance to global ratings of job performance: A policy-capturing approach
entries.main_finding: Raters weight task, citizenship and counterproductive performance differently, forming distinct rating policies.
entries.limitations: Hypothetical profiles; policy capturing may differ from real appraisal.
entries.relevance: Global ratings embed rater-specific weighting policies.
entries.design_implications: Historical overall ratings are treated as biased labels, never as ground truth.

entries.authors: Viswesvaran, C., Ones, D. S., & Schmidt, F. L.
entries.title: Comparative analysis of the reliability of job performance ratings
entries.main_finding: Mean interrater reliability of supervisory ratings of overall job performance was about .52; interrater reliability was lower than intrarater reliability.
entries.limitations: Appropriateness of interrater reliability as the correction coefficient has been debated.
entries.relevance: A single manager's rating carries large rater-specific error.
entries.design_implications: Ratings are audited, not learned from; review notes are qualitative and multi-source.

entries.authors: Scullen, S. E., Mount, M. K., & Goff, M.
entries.title: Understanding the latent structure of job performance ratings
entries.main_finding: Idiosyncratic rater effects accounted for more variance in multisource ratings (about 62% and 53% in two samples) than the ratee's actual performance.
entries.limitations: Developmental multisource ratings of managers; may differ for administrative ratings.
entries.relevance: Motivates Scenario C (rater leniency) and the label audit.
entries.design_implications: Synthetic ratings include rater leniency; MeritVector tests whether rating differences survive context adjustment.

entries.authors: Murphy, K. R.
entries.title: Explaining the weak relationship between job performance and ratings of job performance
entries.main_finding: Ratings are widely viewed as poor measures of performance; systematic non-performance factors and intentional distortion help explain the weak link.
entries.limitations: Focal argument paper with commentaries; not a single empirical estimate.
entries.relevance: Justifies not treating manager ratings or promotions as ground truth.
entries.design_implications: Label audit compares ratings with context-adjusted evidence and activity volume.

entries.authors: Bommer, W. H., Johnson, J. L., Rich, G. A., Podsakoff, P. M., & MacKenzie, S. B.
entries.title: On the interchangeability of objective and subjective measures of employee performance: A meta-analysis
entries.main_finding: Objective and subjective performance measures are related but not interchangeable (a moderate correlation is reported in secondary summaries).
entries.limitations: Effect size reported here from secondary sources, not re-checked against the original tables.
entries.relevance: Objective records and judgements capture different things.
entries.design_implications: Business views show objective evidence and human judgements side by side, never merged into one number.

entries.authors: Cronbach, L. J., & Meehl, P. E.
entries.title: Construct validity in psychological tests
entries.main_finding: Introduces construct validity: a measure is validated by testing a network of theoretical relationships, not by a single criterion.
entries.limitations: Classical framing; later work (Messick) broadened validity to include consequences.
entries.relevance: MeritVector's constructs need nomological-network evidence.
entries.design_implications: VALIDITY_FRAMEWORK lists expected convergent/discriminant relations for each construct and tests them on synthetic data.

entries.authors: Messick, S.
entries.title: Validity of psychological assessment: Validation of inferences from persons' responses and performances as scientific inquiry into score meaning
entries.main_finding: Validity is a unified evaluation of the evidence and consequences supporting inferences from scores, including construct-irrelevant variance and construct under-representation.
entries.limitations: Framework, not a procedure; consequential validity remains debated.
entries.relevance: Context effects are construct-irrelevant variance in raw delivery metrics.
entries.design_implications: Each metric documents intended and prohibited interpretations and its likely construct-irrelevant variance.

entries.authors: Shrout, P. E., & Fleiss, J. L.
entries.title: Intraclass correlations: Uses in assessing rater reliability
entries.main_finding: Defines six forms of the intraclass correlation and guidance for choosing among them.
entries.limitations: Assumes the ANOVA model fits the design.
entries.relevance: Reliability of person-level aggregates (how consistent is a person's evidence across projects?).
entries.design_implications: The research engine reports ICC(1)/ICC(k) for person-level aggregates to show how much evidence a stable estimate needs.

entries.authors: Vandenberg, R. J., & Lance, C. E.
entries.title: A review and synthesis of the measurement invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for organizational research
entries.main_finding: Cross-group comparisons require tests of measurement invariance; proposes an integrative testing sequence.
entries.limitations: Developed for latent-variable (SEM) measures; applies only partially to behavioural records.
entries.relevance: Fairness audits compare groups; indicators must mean the same thing across groups.
entries.design_implications: Fairness audit includes an indicator-structure comparison across groups (invariance-lite), flagged as exploratory.

entries.authors: Podsakoff, P. M., MacKenzie, S. B., Lee, J.-Y., & Podsakoff, N. P.
entries.title: Common method biases in behavioral research: A critical review of the literature and recommended remedies
entries.main_finding: Shared measurement method can inflate or deflate observed relationships; procedural and statistical remedies are reviewed.
entries.limitations: Focused on survey research.
entries.relevance: Stakeholder surveys and manager ratings share rater sources.
entries.design_implications: Evidence from the same source (e.g., one stakeholder) is flagged; perception-based indicators never stand alone.

entries.authors: Strathern, M.
entries.title: 'Improving ratings': Audit in the British University system
entries.main_finding: Anthropological critique of the 'audit explosion': audit procedures take on a life of their own and can jeopardise what they audit (a commonly cited formulation of Goodhart's law is associated with this essay).
entries.limitations: Commentary on higher-education audit; the Goodhart association is secondary attribution.
entries.relevance: Any metric MeritVector surfaces can become a target.
entries.design_implications: No single target metric; activity counts are never rewarded; dashboards emphasise context and uncertainty.

entries.authors: Campbell, D. T.
entries.title: Assessing the impact of planned social change
entries.venue: Evaluation and Program Planning, 2(1), 67–90 (reprinted in Journal of MultiDisciplinary Evaluation, 7(15))
entries.main_finding: Argues for quasi-experimental evaluation of social programmes; source of the observation now called Campbell's law about quantitative indicators being corrupted when used for decisions.
entries.limitations: The DOI is for the open-access reprint; the law's exact wording should be checked in the text.
entries.relevance: Indicator corruption under decision pressure.
entries.design_implications: Assessment indicators are separated from assistance data and not used for automated decisions.

entries.authors: Kerr, S.
entries.title: On the folly of rewarding A, while hoping for B
entries.main_finding: Reward systems often reward behaviours different from those the organisation hopes for.
entries.limitations: Illustrative essay rather than systematic evidence.
entries.relevance: Counting tasks or meetings would reward visible busyness.
entries.design_implications: Activity is stored as context only and demonstrably uncorrelated (or negatively correlated) with adjusted contribution in the simulation.

entries.authors: Bernstein, E. S.
entries.title: The transparency paradox: A role for privacy in organizational learning and operational control
entries.main_finding: In a factory field experiment, reducing observability (zones of privacy) improved performance; close observation led workers to hide productive deviations.
entries.limitations: Single manufacturing setting in China.
entries.relevance: Surveillance can reduce the performance it aims to measure.
entries.design_implications: No covert monitoring; minimal, disclosed data collection; the coordinator is assistance-first.

entries.authors: Ravid, D. M., Tomczak, D. L., White, J. C., & Behrend, T. S.
entries.title: EPM 20/20: A review, framework, and research agenda for electronic performance monitoring
entries.main_finding: Reviews electronic performance monitoring and proposes a framework of monitoring characteristics (purpose, invasiveness, transparency, etc.).
entries.limitations: Narrative review.
entries.relevance: Design characteristics of monitoring shape employee outcomes.
entries.design_implications: Purpose limitation, transparency notices and employee data visibility are implemented as product features.

entries.authors: Simpson, E. H.
entries.title: The interpretation of interaction in contingency tables
entries.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, 13(2), 238–241
entries.main_finding: Aggregated associations can reverse within subgroups (Simpson's paradox).
entries.relevance: Raw on-time rates aggregated across project types can reverse once complexity strata are considered.
entries.design_implications: EDA reports stratified comparisons alongside pooled ones; the flagship experiment demonstrates reversal risk.

entries.authors: Barnett, A. G., van der Pols, J. C., & Dobson, A. J.
entries.title: Regression to the mean: What it is and how to deal with it
entries.main_finding: Extreme measurements tend to be followed by values nearer the mean; design and analysis remedies are described.
entries.relevance: People flagged after an extreme period will 'improve' or 'decline' by chance.
entries.design_implications: Longitudinal flags use shrinkage and FDR control; 'improvement' after a bad period is reported with RTM caveats.

entries.authors: Rubin, D. B.
entries.title: Inference and missing data
entries.main_finding: Formalises when the missing-data mechanism can be ignored (missing at random / ignorability), the basis of the MCAR/MAR/MNAR taxonomy.
entries.relevance: Quality scores and surveys are missing non-randomly in the simulation.
entries.design_implications: Missing-data diagnostics test whether missingness depends on observed context; MNAR risks are stated.

entries.authors: Greenland, S., Pearl, J., & Robins, J. M.
entries.title: Causal diagrams for epidemiologic research
entries.main_finding: Causal diagrams identify which variables must be controlled for unconfounded estimates and expose failures of traditional confounder criteria.
entries.limitations: Requires a correct diagram; unmeasured variables limit identification.
entries.relevance: Assignment of people to projects is confounded by unobserved skill.
entries.design_implications: Causal questions are stated with explicit DAGs; unobserved confounders are listed and sensitivity analysis is mandatory.

entries.authors: VanderWeele, T. J., & Ding, P.
entries.title: Sensitivity analysis in observational research: Introducing the E-value
entries.main_finding: The E-value is the minimum strength of association an unmeasured confounder would need with both treatment and outcome to explain away an observed association.
entries.limitations: Defined on the risk-ratio scale; conversion for continuous outcomes is approximate.
entries.relevance: Quantifies robustness of associations such as resources → delivery.
entries.design_implications: Causal workstream reports E-values (approximate for continuous outcomes, labelled as such).

entries.authors: Cinelli, C., & Hazlett, C.
entries.title: Making sense of sensitivity: Extending omitted variable bias
entries.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, 82(1), 39–67
entries.main_finding: Introduces the robustness value and partial-R² tools for omitted-variable sensitivity computable from regression output.
entries.limitations: Linear models; benchmarking against observed covariates needs care.
entries.relevance: The flagship experiment's omitted-confounder sensitivity.
entries.design_implications: Robustness values are reported for context coefficients in the regression workstream.

entries.authors: Benjamini, Y., & Hochberg, Y.
entries.title: Controlling the false discovery rate: A practical and powerful approach to multiple testing
entries.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, 57(1), 289–300
entries.main_finding: Controls the expected proportion of false discoveries with a simple step-up procedure, gaining power over familywise control.
entries.limitations: Original proof for independent tests.
entries.relevance: Hundreds of per-person trend tests.
entries.design_implications: Per-person flags use BH-FDR; registered hypothesis families use Holm or BH as declared.

entries.authors: Kaufman, S., Rosset, S., Perlich, C., & Stitelman, O.
entries.title: Leakage in data mining: Formulation, detection, and avoidance
entries.venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data, 6(4), Article 15
entries.main_finding: Formalises data leakage and proposes detection and avoidance practices (e.g., timestamps and legitimacy of features at prediction time).
entries.relevance: Milestone-risk classification uses snapshots; features must exist at prediction time.
entries.design_implications: Classifier features are built from point-in-time snapshots and a test asserts every feature timestamp precedes the prediction time.

entries.authors: Hennig, C.
entries.title: Cluster-wise assessment of cluster stability
entries.main_finding: Assesses stability of individual clusters by resampling (Jaccard similarity), the basis of clusterboot.
entries.limitations: Stability does not imply validity or meaningfulness.
entries.relevance: Project-environment clusters must be stable to be reported.
entries.design_implications: Clusters are reported only with bootstrap stability; unstable clusters are labelled exploratory.

entries.authors: Mitchell, M., Wu, S., Zaldivar, A., Barnes, P., Vasserman, L., Hutchinson, B., Spitzer, E., Raji, I. D., & Gebru, T.
entries.title: Model cards for model reporting
entries.main_finding: Proposes model cards documenting intended use, performance across conditions and groups, and limitations.
entries.limitations: Documentation does not guarantee responsible use.
entries.relevance: Every MeritVector model carries a model card.
entries.design_implications: The model registry refuses registration without a complete specification (question, target, use, prohibited use, baselines, leakage controls, limitations).

entries.authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entries.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
entries.main_finding: Voluntary, sector-agnostic framework organised around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage functions for AI risk.
entries.limitations: Voluntary; not employment-specific.
entries.relevance: Structure for MeritVector's risk register and validation gates.
entries.design_implications: Governance docs map controls to Govern/Map/Measure/Manage.

entries.authors: ISO/IEC
entries.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system
entries.main_finding: Requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system.
entries.limitations: Paywalled; certification is organisational, not product-level.
entries.relevance: Future enterprise customers may require alignment.
entries.design_implications: Roadmap item: map MeritVector governance artefacts to an AIMS (v0.4).

entries.authors: European Parliament and Council
entries.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
entries.main_finding: Annex III lists AI used in employment and workers' management (including evaluation of performance and behaviour) among high-risk uses (per legal commentary reviewed; check the official text for exact wording and dates).
entries.limitations: Exact Annex III wording and application dates were not read from EUR-Lex in this session.
entries.relevance: If deployed in the EU, assessment features would likely fall in the high-risk category.
entries.design_implications: Human oversight, logging, transparency and data governance are built in; legal review is required before EU deployment.

entries.authors: Parliament of New South Wales
entries.title: Workplace Surveillance Act 2005 (NSW) No 47
entries.main_finding: Regulates camera, computer and tracking surveillance of employees; computer surveillance generally requires prior written notice (commentary describes a 14-day period and required notice content).
entries.limitations: Notice details summarised from legal commentary; confirm against the Act's text.
entries.relevance: Any connector that monitors computer use in NSW engages the Act.
entries.design_implications: Configurable surveillance notice; no computer-surveillance connectors in v0.1; notice acknowledgement is audited.

entries.authors: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
entries.title: Australian Privacy Principles and the employee records exemption
entries.main_finding: Private-sector handling of employee records for current/former employment is exempt from the APPs in certain circumstances (s 7B(3)); the exemption is narrow, and reform to remove it has been recommended.
entries.limitations: Law reform status not confirmed in this session.
entries.relevance: MeritVector should not rely on the exemption; it designs to APP standards (notice, use limitation, access, correction).
entries.design_implications: Notice, purpose limitation, access and correction workflows exist regardless of the exemption.
